keySource: The key is NYSED's own, read from the Map to the Standards in the released-items PDF and carried into provenance/itemmap_g7-2025.json by tools/extract_item_map.py. tools/merge_content.py re-checks every letter against that file item by item and refuses to build if one disagrees, so the key here cannot drift from the official table or be shifted by one released item. Every constructed-response answer below cites NYSED's own exemplary-response page and is checked against this project's transcription of the same item.

G7-2025/q03_1.png.alt: Answer choice A: a tree diagram with two main courses, each branching to two desserts.
G7-2025/q03_1.png.long: Answer choice A. A tree diagram with a top row labelled Main Course and a bottom row labelled Dessert. Two main courses appear, C and S; F is not shown. C branches down to P and to B, and S branches down to P and to B, giving four endpoints in all.

G7-2025/q03_2.png.alt: Answer choice B: a tree diagram with three main courses, each branching to two desserts.
G7-2025/q03_2.png.long: Answer choice B. A tree diagram with a top row labelled Main Course and a bottom row labelled Dessert. Three main courses appear, C, S and F. Each one branches down to P and to B, giving six endpoints in all.

G7-2025/q03_3.png.alt: Answer choice C: a tree diagram with three main courses whose dessert branches repeat the same letter.
G7-2025/q03_3.png.long: Answer choice C. A tree diagram with a top row labelled Main Course and a bottom row labelled Dessert. Three main courses appear, C, S and F, each with two branches. The two branches from C both end at P, the two branches from S both end at B, and the two branches from F both end at P. There are six endpoints, but no main course is paired with both desserts.

G7-2025/q03_4.png.alt: Answer choice D: a tree diagram with three main courses, each branching to four desserts.
G7-2025/q03_4.png.long: Answer choice D. A tree diagram with a top row labelled Main Course and a bottom row labelled Dessert. Three main courses appear, C, S and F, each with four branches. C branches to P, B, S and F; S branches to P, B, C and F; F branches to P, B, C and S. There are twelve endpoints, and main-course letters appear in the dessert row alongside P and B.
